specification.problem: Distinguish non-isomorphic cospectral regular graphs (G_4(n;n+2) vs G_5(n;n+2), and T_4, T_5) using a multiparticle (fermionic) continuous-time quantum walk, whose adjacency matrix restricted to the antisymmetric subspace differs between the graphs, and using entanglement entropy of coupled harmonic oscillators placed on the nodes.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Generic background construction: the two-fermion antisymmetric-subspace adjacency matrix for a graph A, plus the comparison criterion of spectra and the Gaussian-state entanglement entropy for a harmonic-oscillator network. Explicit G_4/G_5 adjacency matrices, T_4/T_5 constructions, and analytic entropy results are outside scope. No circuit instance is fixed.

symbols.meaning: adjacency matrix of a graph on N vertices
adjacency matrix restricted to the antisymmetric two-fermion subspace
coupling (spring) matrix of the oscillator network
von Neumann entanglement entropy between a subset of oscillators and the rest
symplectic eigenvalues of the reduced covariance matrix

equations.label: Antisymmetric basis state
equations.justification: Standard fermionic antisymmetric basis; the abstract only mentions an antisymmetric fermionic basis.

equations.label: Two-particle Hamiltonian
equations.description: Non-interacting fermion walk generator restricted to the antisymmetric subspace.
equations.justification: Standard construction for non-interacting multiparticle walks; the paper's exact form is not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Distinguishing criterion
equations.description: Cospectral graphs are distinguished if their antisymmetric-subspace matrices differ.
equations.abstract_quote: we rewrite the adjacency matrices of graphs in the antisymmetric fermionic basis and show that they are different for these pairs of graphs
equations.justification: The abstract says the rewritten matrices differ. A spectral comparison is my choice, and the spectrum of A^{(2)} is the pairwise sums of eigenvalues, so it is identical for cospectral graphs. Differences must therefore appear in the matrix structure rather than its spectrum, and the criterion is stated as a matrix difference, with the spectrum clause likely failing for non-interacting fermions.
assumptions: Non-interacting case: spectra of A^{(2)} coincide for cospectral graphs, so a distinction needs matrix-level or graph-structure-dependent invariants such as return probabilities from specific states

equations.label: Oscillator network Hamiltonian
equations.description: Identical harmonic oscillators on the nodes, coupled through the graph.
equations.justification: The abstract says nodes are identical quantum harmonic oscillators; the coupling form is assumed.

equations.label: Entanglement entropy of a Gaussian state
equations.description: Entropy of the reduced Gaussian state of a subset of oscillators.
equations.justification: Standard result for Gaussian states; the paper's analytic expressions are not available.

registers.name: walker_positions
registers.role: Two-fermion position space of dimension N(N-1)/2 in the antisymmetric subspace; no circuit encoding is given

steps.description: Build the adjacency matrices of the two cospectral graphs (explicit G_4, G_5 not available from the abstract).
Form the antisymmetric two-particle basis and matrices A^{(2)}.
Compare A^{(2)} for the two graphs.
For the entropy approach, place oscillators on the nodes, compute the ground-state covariance, reduce to a subset, and compute S for both graphs.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare A^{(2)} matrices (or derived walk quantities) and the entropy values S between G_4 and G_5; different values indicate non-isomorphism.
missing_information: Explicit adjacency structure of G_4(n;n+2), G_5(n;n+2), T_4, T_5
